1 # AGENTS.md: rules for an AI building views with proposal-kit 2 3 A proposal is something a homeowner signs. Every rule below stops a mistake that looks 4 finished on screen and is wrong on paper. Read `components.json` for every prop. 5 6 ## Use only these 7 8 - `Money` for every amount: `` shows $24,900. Pass **whole cents**, never dollars. 9 - `PaymentLine` for every monthly payment: ``. 10 `apr` and `termMonths` are required. The APR and term print on the same line as the payment. 11 - `SavingsEstimate` for every savings figure: 12 ``. 13 It computes the figure, says "Estimated" and prints the assumptions. Do not pass your own savings number. 14 - shadcn/ui `Card`, `Badge`, `Button`, `Separator` from `@/components/ui/*` for layout and status. 15 16 ## Never 17 18 1. Type a currency string (`"$24,900"`, `` `$${price}` ``, `

${price}

`) or format currency yourself 19 (`Intl.NumberFormat` or `toLocaleString` with `style: "currency"`). Use `Money`. 20 2. Show a monthly payment ("/mo", "per month") without `PaymentLine`. 21 3. # AGENTS.md: rules for an AI building views with proposal-kit A proposal is something a homeowner signs. Every rule below stops a mistake that looks finished on screen and is wrong on paper. Read `components.json` for every prop. ## Use only these - `Money` for every amount: `` shows $24,900. Pass **whole cents**, never dollars. - `PaymentLine` for every monthly payment: ``. `apr` and `termMonths` are required. The APR and term print on the same line as the payment. - `SavingsEstimate` for every savings figure: ``. It computes the figure, says "Estimated" and prints the assumptions. Do not pass your own savings number. - shadcn/ui `Card`, `Badge`, `Button`, `Separator` from `@/components/ui/*` for layout and status. ## Never 1. Type a currency string (`"$24,900"`, `` `$${price}` ``, `

${price}

`) or format currency yourself (`Intl.NumberFormat` or `toLocaleString` with `style: "currency"`). Use `Money`. 2. Show a monthly payment ("/mo", "per month") without `PaymentLine`. 3. Use a hex, rgb or px value, an inline style size, an arbitrary value like `text-[#0d5c48]`, or a Tailwind palette class like `bg-green-500` (the palette is switched off, so it would render unstyled). Use the token classes: `bg-background`, `bg-card`, `bg-muted`, `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border`, `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, `bg-success text-success-foreground`, `bg-estimate text-estimate-foreground`. Spacing, type and radius classes (`p-4`, `text-sm`, `rounded-lg`) are tokens too. 4. Show savings without `SavingsEstimate`, drop the word "Estimated", or hide the assumptions. 5. Show a status by color alone. Use `Ready to sign`. Use one `h1`, then `h2` per card. Keep text on token colors; they are all 4.5:1 or better in light and dark. Do not mention tax credits, rebates or incentive amounts. ## Data Keep amounts as whole cents in one data object at the top of the file. Derive totals from it (line items add up to the price; price minus down payment is the amount financed), so every number on the page comes from the same source. ## Check `npm run check` runs TypeScript (required props), ESLint with the `proposal-kit/*` rules, the token check and the tests. A view is done when it passes.

I've written the summary page to `src/views/GeneratedSummary.tsx`. I couldn't run commands here, so it hasn't been type-checked, linted or rendered yet. Running `npm run check` is the next step.

**What's on the page:** a heading for Maria Okafor with the address, installer, proposal number and date, plus a "Ready to sign" badge with a check icon (so status isn't shown by color alone). Below that are four cards:
- **Your system:** panels, size, inverters and yearly production.
- **Price:** the three line items, total price, down payment and amount financed.
- **Loan:** the monthly payment with its APR and term, and the total of all 240 payments.
- **Bill savings:** the estimated savings, labelled "Estimated" with its assumptions printed underneath.

**How the numbers are produced:** all the inputs are in one data object at the top of the file, with amounts in cents. The page works out everything else from those inputs instead of typing it in:
- **Size and price:** 7.38 kW comes from 18 × 410 W. The $22,000 total is the sum of the line items, and $20,000 financed is the total minus the down payment.
- **Loan:** the $149.00 payment is calculated with the project's existing loan formula (`monthlyPaymentCents`), and the $35,760 total is that payment × 240.
- **Savings:** the savings component calculates the figures itself and gets $1,785 for the first year and about $65,080 over 25 years.

All of these match the numbers you gave. One assumption in the savings estimate: it treats production as a flat 11,900 kWh every year and doesn't account for panels producing less as they age. That's how your $65,080 figure was worked out too.

The page follows the project's AGENTS.md rules: all amounts go through `Money`, the payment through `PaymentLine` and savings through `SavingsEstimate`. It uses only the project's color and style classes, has one `h1` with an `h2` per card, and doesn't mention tax credits.

**Things to check:**
- **"Review and sign" button:** it isn't connected to anything yet, because I didn't find a signing flow in the project to link it to.
- **"Total of 240 payments" row:** I put it right below the payment line in the same card, so the APR and term are always nearby. I couldn't see the source of the `payment-needs-terms` lint rule, though, so it might still flag the word "payments" in that label.
- **Reference page:** `components.json` points to `src/views/ProposalSummary.tsx` as the example page, but that file doesn't exist. I followed AGENTS.md instead.

- **Loan:** the $149.00 payment is calculated with the project's existing loan formula (`monthlyPaymentCents`), and the $35,760 total is that payment × 240.
- **Savings:** the savings component calculates the figures itself and gets $1,785 for the first year and about $65,080 over 25 years.
